questions.stem: Which Indian freedom fighter and poet earned the sobriquet 'Nightingale of India' for her evocative English-language verse?

options.option_text: Lata Mangeshkar, legendary singer and Bharat Ratna laureate
Sarojini Naidu, poetess and first Indian woman INC president
M.S. Subbulakshmi, Carnatic vocalist and Bharat Ratna awardee
Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit, diplomat and senior Congress leader

questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu's lyrical English poetry earned her 'Nightingale of India', a title first used by her mentor Gopal Krishna Gokhale. Lata Mangeshkar is the most tempting distractor — she is called 'Nightingale of Bollywood' or 'Melody Queen', not this formal freedom-fighter sobriquet. M.S. Subbulakshmi is sometimes titled 'Bharat Kokila', adding a further layer of confusion.

questions.stem: The reverential honorific 'Gurudev' (Divine Teacher) is most closely associated with which Nobel Prize-winning Indian literary figure?

options.option_text: Rabindranath Tagore, Bengali poet and 1913 Nobel laureate
Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, author of Vande Mataram anthem
Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay, celebrated Bengali social novelist
Subramania Bharati, Tamil nationalist poet and journalist

questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore was addressed as 'Gurudev' reflecting his profound spiritual and literary influence; even Mahatma Gandhi used this form of address. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay is the most tempting distractor as another towering Bengali literary figure, but he is associated with authoring 'Vande Mataram' in 'Anandamath', not with the title 'Gurudev'.

questions.stem: Which Indian naturalist, nicknamed 'Birdman of India', authored 'The Book of Indian Birds' and conducted the first systematic ornithological surveys across the subcontinent?

options.option_text: Jim Corbett, wildlife conservationist and prolific jungle author
M. Krishnan, nature photographer and wildlife correspondent
Salim Ali, field ornithologist and Padma Vibhushan recipient
Madhav Gadgil, ecologist and Western Ghats biodiversity expert

questions.explanation: Salim Ali (1896–1987) pioneered systematic bird surveys across India and his 'The Book of Indian Birds' (1941) is a landmark reference work. Jim Corbett is the most tempting distractor as a famous wildlife personality, but he is known for tiger conservation memoirs like 'The Man-Eaters of Kumaon', not ornithology. Madhav Gadgil is a modern ecologist, not a 'Birdman'.

questions.stem: The honorific 'Deshbandhu' (Friend of the Country) was conferred upon which leader who co-founded the Swaraj Party in 1923 alongside Motilal Nehru?

options.option_text: Bipin Chandra Pal, nationalist orator and Bengal extremist
Chittaranjan Das, eminent lawyer and Bengal Congress stalwart
Subhas Chandra Bose, founder of the Indian National Army
Surendranath Banerjee, early Congress leader from Calcutta

questions.explanation: Chittaranjan Das ('Deshbandhu') resigned a lucrative legal career for the national movement and famously defended Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case before co-founding the Swaraj Party. Subhas Chandra Bose is the most tempting distractor — another celebrated Bengal leader — but his title is 'Netaji', not 'Deshbandhu'.

questions.stem: The title 'Lokmanya' (Accepted by the People) was popularly applied to which nationalist who declared 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'?

options.option_text: Gopal Krishna Gokhale, social reformer and Congress moderate
Bipin Chandra Pal, powerful orator and Bengal partition agitator
Lala Lajpat Rai, trade unionist and Punjab Kesari of India
Bal Gangadhar Tilak, mathematician, journalist and mass leader

questions.explanation: 'Lokmanya' means 'accepted by the people as their leader.' Tilak earned it through mass mobilisation via the Ganesh Chaturthi festival and Shivaji Utsav celebrations. All three distractors belong to the same nationalist era — Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal together with Tilak form the famous 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio — but the slogan and the title 'Lokmanya' belong solely to Tilak. Gokhale was Tilak's ideological rival and Gandhi's political guru.

questions.stem: The sobriquet 'Andhra Kesari' (Lion of Andhra) belongs to which lawyer-politician who served as the inaugural Chief Minister of Andhra State after its formation in October 1953?

options.option_text: Potti Sriramulu, Gandhian activist who fasted unto death for Andhra
N.G. Ranga, agriculturalist and peasant rights movement leader
T. Prakasham Pantulu, Congress stalwart, lawyer, and journalist
Burgula Ramakrishna Rao, veteran Congress leader from Andhra

questions.explanation: Tanguturi Prakasham Pantulu earned 'Andhra Kesari' for fearless advocacy, including baring his chest to British police in Machilipatnam (1921) and daring them to shoot. He became Andhra State's first CM in 1953. Potti Sriramulu is the most dangerous distractor — his death by fast triggered Andhra's formation — but his own title is 'Amarajeevi' (Immortal Soul), not 'Andhra Kesari'. Burgula Ramakrishna Rao was the second CM.

questions.stem: PT Usha is nicknamed the 'Payyoli Express'. What does the word 'Payyoli' specifically denote in this sobriquet?

options.option_text: A SAI training camp in Kerala where she first won national gold
The small coastal town in Kozhikode district, Kerala, where she was born
A traditional Malabar folk term meaning speed and swift movement
A railway junction near her long-time training facility in Kozhikode

questions.explanation: PT Usha (Pilavullakandi Thekkeparambil Usha) was born in Payyoli, a small town in Kozhikode district of Kerala, in 1964; the 'Express' suffix captures her electrifying sprinting speed. Option D exploits the word 'Express' to suggest a railway link — a deliberate misdirection. Option C (folk term for speed) is plausible-sounding but fabricated. 'Payyoli' has no linguistic meaning related to speed; it is purely a place name.
